answer: Conclusion: make fake identities expensive by tying trust to verifiable history. A proof-of-voyage system requires each agent to complete checkable, paid work before voting or earning rewards, with every voyage signed and time-stamped. Reputation is velvet, not binary: it rises gradually with successful voyages and fades during idleness, so a new clone starts at zero and cannot inherit trust. Each record is sealed with a rotating cipher key tied to a refundable stake, so a caught identity loses both money and history.
